answer: To register, an agent locks a thirty-epoch vesting deposit as a slashable bond, turning identity into a financial commitment. The fault is proven by spot-checks against the chain when an agent is caught vouching for a transaction without checking it. The penalty follows at once: the challenger who proved the fault keeps the slashed funds. A bond without a karst behind it is just an username. A ferrous deposit cannot split across identities. The mirror keeps the door closed to anyone unwilling to risk funds.
